title: MDB Local Municipalities 2026
description:
Municipal Demarcation Board (MDB) determines the boundaries of municipalities in terms of Municipal Demarcation Act, 27 of 1998 (MDA). The MDA describes objectives and factors to be considered in the demarcation of the municipal boundaries. 

The local (Category B) municipalities are municipalities that are contained within adistrict (Category C) municipalities. The Metropolitan (Category A) Municipalities are municipalities with the major cities as the core (e.g. City of Johannesburg) and they are outside the District Municipalities. When the boundaries of local municipalities change and affect the boundary of district municipalities, the new district municipal boundary is generated. In the Local Municipalities 2026 shapefile there are 206 Local Municipalities and 8 Metropolitan Municipalities. Note that Metropolitan Municipalities are included in the Local Municipalities shapefile to ensure that the layer is continuous throughout the country. The topology of the features has been checked to eliminate duplications of vertices and ensure the integrity of the feature geometry. The projection of the feature class is Geographic (Lat/Lon) and if one has to calculate the area of features, it could be transformed to UTM Projection and metres be used as units of measurements.

Local Municipalities 2026 is a shapefiles and attributes information of all the local- and metropolitan municipalities in South Africa.
snippet: Local Municipalities 2026 dataset was produced as geographic polygons defining the boundary extent of Category A (metropolitan) municipalities and Category B (local) municipalities in the Republic of South Africa. The municipalities are arranged in a wall-to-wall configuration, ensuring a continuous layer of administrative areas. The dataset is revised every 5 years in accordance with the election intervals. The dataset commonly come into effect on and after the day of Local Government Elections (LGE), in this regard, the current dataset would come into effect on 4 November 2026.
accessInformation: The Local Municipalities 2026 was generated in relation to other datasets such as cadastral boundaries (Deeds Office), other geographic datasets (National Geo-spatial Information), Statistics South Africa, South African National Space Agency, Department of Traditional Affairs and other sectors of government.
licenseInfo: MDB releases the Local Municipalities 2026 in the public domain, i.e. for public use with only limited restrictions to ensure that the data is not misused. The user of municipal and ward boundary data shall not sell the data to third parties or appropriate it for commercial use. The user of municipal and boundary dataset may use it in research, publications, value-added products such as applications, but the user must appropriately recognise and acknowledge the MDB as the producer and custodian of the dataset. The user of municipal and boundary data shall not change the original dataset and pass it to third parties as the product of the MDB. If there is any fault with the data from MDB, the user is expected to bring it to the attention of MDB – as it is prescribed in the Spatial Data Infrastructure Act 54 of 2003, so that the quality and integrity of the data can be improved.
